population_definition: all kernels in shard FV-PROPFLOOR-SHARD-B26-1, enumerated below by kernel id and spec digest
independence_sentence: Each item listed was reviewed and attested independently; the single signature is a mechanical convenience over the enumerated digests, not a bulk review.
per_item_basis_of_review: Every row ran the same two mechanical checks unconditionally: (1) the fixture-oracle gate — compute() output diffed against the kernel's own existing golden fixtures before any property was trusted, and (2) run-proptests.mjs green (process exit 0). ULP-boundary forcing was mandatory and present for the float-sensitive rows named in the WU (art-540, art-547, art-550), and float:no exception boundary cases (forced categorical) were used for the remaining 7. ⚠ TWO ROWS WERE RECLASSIFIED DURING AUTHORING per the WU's FIX-2 CARRY instruction ('verify float-sensitivity ... not inherited from the triage table alone'): the WU listed art-549-g20-corridor-cost-gap and art-580-15c3-3a-note-h-margin-debit as float-sensitive, but direct measurement against the shipped kernel source found art-549's only arithmetic is integer subtraction of two Number.isSafeInteger-constrained basis-point values (gap_bps = observed - target, no multiplication/division anywhere in compute() — the kernel's own docstring states this explicitly), and art-580's only numeric operation is Math.min() of two Number.isSafeInteger-constrained minor-unit values (no multiplication/division/rounding). Neither kernel has a float-precision failure mode to force ULP cases against, so both were treated as float:no exceptions with forced categorical boundary cases instead (tie-at-min, zero, negative, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER cases for art-580; exact-threshold, one-bps-over/under, negative-rejected cases for art-549) and this correction is the load-bearing content of this basis-of-review paragraph, not a footnote. The actually float-sensitive trio (art-540's reserve_to_liability_ratio division, art-547's qty*rate multiplication with round2, art-550's Math.round((net*rate)/1e6) — the last explicitly IEEE-754-double per its own docstring) carry genuine ULP-boundary forcing: threshold-at-exactly-1.0, near-zero denominator, negative zero, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER-scale multiplication precision loss, and .5-tie rounding cases. No row beyond these mechanical checks received a separate in-depth human review in this pass — that is exactly the gap human_sign_off.status=PENDING names.

ulp_forcing_summary: 3 of 10 kernels carry genuine ULP-boundary forcing (art-540, art-547, art-550), confirmed float-sensitive by reading the kernel source. 7 of 10 carry forced categorical boundary cases instead: 5 were float:no per the WU row as authored (art-527, art-545, art-546, art-551, art-581), and 2 were RECLASSIFIED from float:yes to float:no during authoring per the WU's FIX-2 CARRY instruction (art-549-g20-corridor-cost-gap — integer bps subtraction only, no division; art-580-15c3-3a-note-h-margin-debit — Math.min of two safe integers only, no multiplication/division). Both reclassifications are checked in their items above with the specific arithmetic evidence, not asserted.
